title: Disaggregated Prefill/Decode — NVIDIA Dynamo and llm-d

questions.question: Which expression supplies prefill time in ms_colocated and ms_disaggregated?
questions.explanation: Both functions compute prefill_ms as prompt / PREFILL_TOK_PER_MS, using the 40 tokens/ms constant.

questions.question: For 4,096 prompt tokens, how large is the RDMA KV transfer in this toy model?
questions.explanation: 4,096 × 125,000 bytes = 512,000,000 bytes = 0.512 GB; at 100 GB/s the transfer takes about 5.12 ms.

questions.question: Which decode rate is used for the memory-optimized disaggregated GPU pool?
questions.explanation: DECODE_TOK_PER_MS_DECODE_GPU is 0.18; colocated decode uses the slower 0.10 tokens/ms constant.

questions.question: Why is TCP transfer slower than the NIXL RDMA path in ms_disaggregated?
options: TCP skips the KV transfer entirely
RDMA adds a second prefill pass
TCP uses a larger decode GPU
questions.explanation: The transfer time divides the same KV bytes by the transport bandwidth; TCP's 10 GB/s constant is one tenth of RDMA's 100 GB/s.

questions.question: With output tokens held fixed, what does increasing prompt length do to disaggregated serving?
options: It removes prefill work from both paths
It increases KV transfer time, weakening the disaggregated advantage
It makes decode throughput independent of output length
questions.explanation: With output fixed, prompt tokens add KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_70B_FP8 to the transfer term in ms_disaggregated, while the decode-time difference stays fixed; the extra transfer therefore weakens the advantage.

questions.question: What KV size per prompt token does the 70B FP8 fixture use?
questions.explanation: The constant KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_70B_FP8 is 125,000 bytes; multiplying it by prompt gives the transferred KV payload.
